title: “And how, monks, does a monk dwell ‘as below, so above; as above, so below’? Here, monks, a monk contemplates this body from the soles…
content: “And how, monks, does a monk dwell ‘as below, so above; as above, so below’? Here, monks, a monk contemplates this body from the soles of the feet upward, from the top of the head downward, enclosed by skin and full of various impurities: ‘There are in this body: head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, intestinal mesentery, stomach, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, skin oil, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine.’ Thus, monks, a monk dwells ‘as below, so above; as above, so below.’”

title: “One who does not go too far, Nor lag behind, Having overcome all this unreality — That monk abandons the near and far shore, Like…
content:
“One who does not go too far,
Nor lag behind,
Having overcome all this unreality —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One who does not go too far,
Nor lag behind,
Knowing that all this is unreality —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One who does not go too far,
Nor lag behind,
Free from greed, free from hatred,
Free from delusion —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

title: “‘For life, the arahants have abandoned unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. Today, this night and day,…
content: “‘For life, the arahants have abandoned unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. Today, this night and day, I too abandon unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. In this factor, I follow the arahants and will observe the uposatha day.’ This is the third factor attained.”

title: “Monks, while Prince Vipassī was going to the pleasure garden, he saw a sick person, suffering, gravely ill, wallowing in his own urine and feces,…
content: “Monks, while Prince Vipassī was going to the pleasure garden, he saw a sick person, suffering, gravely ill, wallowing in his own urine and feces, needing others to lift him, needing others to support him. Seeing this, the prince asked the charioteer: ‘Good man, what has this person done that his eyes are not like those of others, his voice not like others?’ ‘Your Highness, that is called a sick person.’ ‘Good man, why is he called a sick person?’ ‘Your Highness, he is called a sick person because he has not recovered from his illness.’ ‘Good man, then am I subject to sickness, not having fallen sick yet?’ ‘Your Highness, you and I as well — all of us are subject to sickness, even though we have not fallen sick yet.’ ‘Good man, then this visit to the pleasure garden is enough. Drive back to the palace.’ ‘Yes, Your Highness.’ Monks, the charioteer, obeying the prince, drove back to the palace. Monks, Prince Vipassī returned to the palace, suffering, grieving, and thought: ‘Shameful indeed is this birth! And anyone who is born must also age, must also be sick!’”

title: “Monks, form is suffering, both in the past and in the future, not to mention the present. Seeing this, monks, a well-taught noble disciple has…
content: “Monks, form is suffering, both in the past and in the future, not to mention the present. Seeing this, monks, a well-taught noble disciple has no regret for past form, does not delight in future form, and practices disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation regarding present form. Feeling is suffering … Perception is suffering … Formations are suffering … Consciousness is suffering, both in the past and in the future, not to mention the present. Seeing this, monks, a well-taught noble disciple has no regret for past consciousness, does not delight in future consciousness, and practices disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation regarding present consciousness.”

title: “Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But,…
content: “Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But, venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition for the defilement of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively suffering, immersed in suffering, accompanied by suffering, not accompanied by happiness, beings would not become lustful for form. But because form is happiness, Mahāli, immersed in happiness, accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by suffering, beings become lustful for form. Through lust, they are bound; through being bound, they are defiled. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings. Such being the cause, such being the condition, beings are defiled.”

title: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
content: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, consciousness becomes established. When consciousness is established and grows, there is a leaning (nati). When there is a leaning, there is a going to a state of rebirth. When there is a going to a state of rebirth, there is future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Such is the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no leaning. When there is no leaning, there is no going to a state of rebirth. When there is no going to a state of rebirth, there is no future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: Elder Bhalliya: “Who drives away the army of Death, As a great flood sweeps away a frail bridge of reeds — Victorious, fearless, Having subdued,…
content:
Elder Bhalliya:
“Who drives away the army of Death,
As a great flood sweeps away a frail bridge of reeds —
Victorious, fearless,
Having subdued, he dwells at peace.”

title: Elder Nun Sumedhā: “What is this foul, stinking body, Frightening, A leather bag full of corpses, Oozing impurities? What is this body I know —…
content:
Elder Nun Sumedhā:

“What is this foul, stinking body,
Frightening,
A leather bag full of corpses,
Oozing impurities?

What is this body I know —
Disgusting, smeared with flesh and blood,
A dwelling for worms,
Food for birds —
This body is like that —
To whom should I give it now?

The body, thrown in a charnel ground,
Not long, loses consciousness —
Like a discarded log —
Relatives are disgusted.

That body thrown in the charnel ground,
Becomes food for others —
Formerly they washed it clean,
Now they are disgusted —
Even parents are like that —
What to say of ordinary people?

They are infatuated with a body without core,
Bound by sinews and bones,
Full of saliva and tears,
Full of feces and urine, foul-smelling.

If this body were cut open,
Its inner parts revealed,
Even one’s mother would be disgusted,
Unable to bear the stench.

It is because of aggregates, elements, and sense-bases
That this body is constituted —
The root of renewed existence, suffering —
They speak of it rightly —
They do not delight in it at all.
So who would I wish to marry?

Even a hundred spears every day,
Constantly piercing the body —
Though harmed for a hundred years —
That would still be better,
Because that suffering,
In the end, would be destroyed.

The wise would agree to such killing,
As the Teacher declared —
They wander on for a long time,
With minds given to killing,
Continually following one after another.

In the realms of devas and humans,
Animals, asuras,
Hungry ghosts, and hell —
They undergo endless slaughter.

In hell, there are many —
Those with defiled minds, fallen —
The heavenly realm is no refuge —
There is no Nibbāna-like happiness there.

Those who attain Nibbāna
Are intimately connected
With the teaching
Of the One with Ten Powers —
At ease, unruffled,
Striving to end birth and death.

Today, father, I am determined to leave.
These empty possessions
Are of no value.
I am disgusted with sensual pleasures,
I am weary of sensual pleasures —
They have been cut off,
Like a palm tree stump.”

title: Then the Blessed One, knowing “This is Māra the Evil One,” recited this verse to Māra: Forms, sounds, tastes, and smells, And all contacts, all…
content:
Then the Blessed One, knowing “This is Māra the Evil One,” recited this verse to Māra:
Forms, sounds, tastes, and smells,
And all contacts, all phenomena —
These are terrifying things,
Bewildering beings in the world.
A disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
Mindful, transcends them all,
Transcending Māra’s power,
Shining like the sun.
